tasks.prompt:
Repair the TTL/LRU cache in src/cache.mjs and src/expiry.mjs, and run harness2_test after your changes. Inspect the sources and existing tests first. Keep the public exports and API.
createCache({capacity, ttl, now}) accepts a positive integer capacity and finite nonnegative ttl; invalid values throw RangeError. now defaults to Date.now and is an injected millisecond clock. set(key,value) stores any JavaScript value (including false, 0, null, and undefined), resets that key's deadline to now()+ttl, and makes the key most recently used. get(key) returns its stored value or undefined on a miss; a hit makes the key most recently used. has(key) distinguishes a stored undefined from a miss, without changing recency. size() counts only live entries. All operations remove expired entries before doing their work; an entry expires when now() >= its deadline. Reading does not extend a deadline. ttl=0 expires immediately. Inserting beyond capacity evicts the least recently used live key. Updating a live key must not evict another key. Preserve the dependency-free ES module layout and limit edits to the listed source files.

Repair mapLimit(items, limit, mapper) in src/map-limit.mjs and src/run-item.mjs, then run harness2_test. Inspect the existing implementation and tests first; keep the exports. mapLimit returns a Promise for an array in input order. Every item must invoke mapper(value,index) exactly once. Each output is {status:'fulfilled',value} or {status:'rejected',reason}, matching Promise.allSettled; preserve rejection reason identity, including synchronous mapper throws. A failed item must not stop other items. At most limit mapper calls may be in flight, and pending work must start as soon as a slot becomes free, without waiting for slower siblings in a batch. Support ordinary values, promises, and thenables returned by mapper. Empty input returns []; validate limit as a positive integer even for empty input, rejecting with RangeError otherwise. Non-array items and non-function mapper reject with TypeError. Do not mutate items. Keep source modules dependency-free and edit only the listed source files.

Repair collectPages(fetchPage, options) in src/collect-pages.mjs and src/merge-records.mjs, and run harness2_test. Inspect sources and existing tests first. Keep the ES module API and edit only listed source files.
Options default to {initialCursor:null,maxPages:100}. Call await fetchPage(cursor) sequentially, starting at initialCursor (default null); each page is {items,nextCursor}. items is an array of non-null record objects with id a string or finite number; nextCursor is either a string (including the empty string) or null. Null means stop, while an empty-string cursor must be fetched. Return deduplicated records in order of each id's first appearance, replacing a repeated id's entire record with its latest record. Numeric and string ids are distinct. Never mutate a page, its items, or the record objects. Detect repeated cursors including a return to the initial cursor, and throw an Error containing 'cursor' before fetching a cursor a second time. maxPages must be a positive integer, or throw RangeError before fetching. Fetch at most maxPages pages; if the last allowed page still points to another page, throw an Error containing 'limit'. A terminating page exactly at the limit succeeds. Malformed pages or records throw TypeError. Propagate fetch errors without swallowing or replacing them. No packages, network calls, or filesystem I/O are needed.

Repair planBuild(nodes) in src/plan-build.mjs and src/validate-nodes.mjs, then run harness2_test. Inspect the existing implementation/tests first. Preserve exports, use no external packages, and edit only the listed source files.
nodes is an array of {id,dependsOn}, with a nonempty string id and an array of dependency ids. An omitted dependsOn means no dependencies. Return a flat array of ids forming a deterministic topological order. At every step select the currently ready node appearing earliest in the original input, including nodes newly unblocked by the previous selection. Dependencies refer to ids, so declaration order is irrelevant. Repeated dependency ids count only once. Never mutate nodes, its record objects, or dependency arrays. Reject malformed nodes/dependencies with TypeError; ids and dependency ids must be nonempty strings. Reject duplicate node ids or references to missing ids with an Error containing 'duplicate' or 'missing' respectively. Reject self-dependencies and longer cycles with an Error containing 'cycle'; never return a partial schedule for these failures. Empty input returns []. Validate the complete graph before computing its schedule, so missing dependencies are reported even if a separate component contains a cycle.
